correctness.rationale: The formal concept extents of the stated two-sorted relation are precisely intersections of closed tree neighborhoods. For distinct centers the intersection is an edge-pair, a unique middle singleton, or the empty set according to distances one, two, or at least three. This proves the exhaustive star/nonstar normal form and rank polynomial; intrinsic rank-one/rank-two incidences reconstruct vertices and edges, and joins recover the remaining rank-three elements, yielding the exact automorphism group. A diameter-four path contains an explicit nonmodular triple. For diameter-three double stars an explicit sublattice of the modular subspace lattice of four-dimensional rational space proves modularity; stars are height two. Diamond sublattices and the grid representation of the four-vertex path settle distributivity. The standard-library checker independently generated all labeled trees of orders three through seven (18,247 instances) and validated normal form, rank and reconstruction; 1,895 lattice-law instances passed. Finite checks are corroboration, not infinite proofs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Rawson et al. dominate the generic correspondence between concept extents and hyperedge intersections but not the specialized all-tree classification. The 2014 bipartite-distance-hereditary theorem characterizes when a Galois-lattice proper part is tree-shaped; this is a different hypothesis and conclusion. General reduced-context theory may imply parts of reconstruction; the claimed main modularity cutoff and explicit rank-four normal form are not supplied by those results. Path contexts are a restricted subfamily, not a dominating parameter regime.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Known general results show that extent sets are neighborhood intersections and sometimes that incidence data are recoverable from a reduced context. Even granting those stronger generic facts, the rank-two reconstruction algorithm and rank polynomial require the tree-specific intersection analysis, while the modularity iff diameter≤3 classification requires the explicit nonmodular triple and modular embedding. The inspected texts do not imply that combined exact statement. The similarly named graph closed-set lattice is inapplicable because it closes under pairs of open-neighborhood intersections rather than being the meet closure generated by the closed neighborhoods.

originality.rationale: The mathematical contribution assessed is the complete rank-four closed-neighborhood normal form for arbitrary finite trees and sharp diameter-three modularity classification, with explicit unlabeled tree reconstruction and automorphism identification. The generic hypergraph-intersection correspondence is credited to Rawson et al. (2023); general reduced-context principles and path specializations are not presented as separately new. Inspected primary work on bipartite distance-hereditary Galois lattices addresses a different classification. An older graph closed-set lattice uses a different closure rule. Targeted searches and result comparison did not identify a covering theorem, but equivalence under historical alternative terminology is a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent tree-specific statement may exist in older neighborhood-hypergraph, bipartite Galois lattice, or context-reduction terminology not indexed by the searched phrases.
The complete text of the 1985 Koh–Poh source was not inspected; the separate closure definition is supported by a later reviewed source, but unknown unrelated material cannot be excluded.

Concept-lattice reconstruction from reduced contexts is established in general. The explicit reconstruction here is a supporting consequence, not a claim of discovering the generic reconstruction principle.
Priority is not independently verified; mathematical correctness does not establish historical novelty.

value.rationale: The theorem completely classifies a natural infinite family of symmetric graph-derived formal contexts, giving an exact linear-size lattice census, a palindromic rank polynomial, lossless reconstruction of arbitrary branched trees from unlabeled lattice order, an exact automorphism group, and a sharp diameter-three algebraic threshold. The finite tree’s detailed branching is invisible in the rank histogram but recoverable from the rank-one/rank-two incidence graph. This is structurally motivated and useful as a reference family for concept-lattice compressibility and identity testing, not a mere isolated computation or arbitrary finite parameter slice.
